\section*{AP \({ }^{\text {® }}\) CALCULUS AB \\ 2009 SCORING GUIDELINES (Form B)}

\section*{Question 1}

At a certain height, a tree trunk has a circular cross section. The radius \(R(t)\) of that cross section grows at a rate modeled by the function
\[
\frac{d R}{d t}=\frac{1}{16}\left(3+\sin \left(t^{2}\right)\right) \text { centimeters per year }
\]
for \(0 \leq t \leq 3\), where time \(t\) is measured in years. At time \(t=0\), the radius is 6 centimeters. The area of the cross section at time \(t\) is denoted by \(A(t)\).
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] Write an expression, involving an integral, for the radius \(R(t)\) for \(0 \leq t \leq 3\). Use your expression to find \(R(3)\).
\item[(b)] Find the rate at which the cross-sectional area \(A(t)\) is increasing at time \(t=3\) years. Indicate units of measure.
\item[(c)] Evaluate \(\int_{0}^{3} A^{\prime}(t) d t\). Using appropriate units, interpret the meaning of that integral in terms of crosssectional area.
\item[(a)] \(R(t)=6+\int_{0}^{t} \frac{1}{16}\left(3+\sin \left(x^{2}\right)\right) d x\)
\[
R(3)=6.610 \text { or } 6.611
\]
\item[(b)] \(A(t)=\pi(R(t))^{2}\)
\[
\begin{aligned}
& A^{\prime}(t)=2 \pi R(t) R^{\prime}(t) \\
& A^{\prime}(3)=8.858 \mathrm{~cm}^{2} / \text { year }
\end{aligned}
\]
\item[(c)] \(\int_{0}^{3} A^{\prime}(t) d t=A(3)-A(0)=24.200\) or 24.201
From time \(t=0\) to \(t=3\) years, the crosssectional area grows by 24.201 square centimeters.
\item[3] : \(\left\{\begin{array}{l}1 \text { : integral } \\ 1: \text { expression for } R(t) \\ 1: R(3)\end{array}\right.\)
\item[] \(3:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: \text { expression for } A(t) \\ 1: \text { expression for } A^{\prime}(t) \\ 1: \text { answer with units }\end{array}\right.\)
\item[3] : \(\left\{\begin{array}{l}1 \text { : uses Fundamental Theorem of Calculus } \\ 1 \text { : value of } \int_{0}^{3} A^{\prime}(t) d t \\ 1 \text { : meaning of } \int_{0}^{3} A^{\prime}(t) d t\end{array}\right.\)
\end{itemize}
